IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: We regularly inspect trees near overhead power lines to keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. A recent inspection found some trees have grown too close to power lines. If unmanaged, branches could touch the overhead lines and cause unexpected interruptions to your electricity supply. We appreciate your area has been impacted with unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. We need to trim these trees, which requires a temporary power cut because the work cannot be done safely while electricity lines are live. This essential work involves approximately 200 metres of tree cutting across 10 sections of the overhead electricity network. We have planned this work for a Saturday so it can be completed safely while the existing Network Rail Road closure is in place. By coordinating the work with this closure, we can avoid the need for an additional road closure at a later date and minimise further disruption to the local community. This work is taking place along Buckhurst Road.

Our staff have now confirmed that our substation equipment has operated due to an underground cable fault which we'll need to pinpoint, excavate, and repair. However, once they've assessed further, we'll let you know if the time frame needs to change. For more information about this type of fault; here's a short video https://UKPN.short.gy/UG - I'll keep you updated.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Aaron at 08:32 - Some customers have told us that they want to be notified about a power cut before it happens. We're sorry we couldn't give you advance notice about this power cut. The issue happened suddenly and without warning, leaving us with no time to alert customers.
Our electricity network is regularly inspected and maintained to help prevent outages, but occasionally an unexpected fault can lead to an unplanned power cut. It's similar to a car that's been fully serviced and passed its MOT but still breaks down without warning.
Thank you for your understanding and we will keep you updated about todays outage until you are restored.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Aaron at 08:24 - Thanks for bearing with us today.

Our engineers are checking our substation equipment to ensure our network is healthy before they attempt to restore your power. They may also walk our cabling route throughout the area to check for any visible problems, check smaller electrical sites in the area, or apply specialist equipment which may restore power temporarily to help them with their testing.

We know that our customers may be worried about the food in the fridge and freezer, so we want to try and help with advice. Food should keep for up to 4 hours in the fridge, and between 24-48 hours in the freezer if you avoid opening them.

We'll keep you updated on our engineers progress.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team
